title.narrative: Primary Education Equity in Learning Program

description.narrative: The development objective of First Phase of Green Agricultural and Rural Revitalization Program for China is to enhance environmentally sustainable agricultural and rural infrastructure development in selected areas of Guangxi and Guizhou. In 2017, the Chinese government adopted an ambitious national RRP, which is implemented in phases of five-year RRS plans. The national RRS plan provides the overarching rural development vision and broadly defined actions. The RRS plans are framed around the “Three rurals”: agriculture, rural areas, and farmers. The main objectives of the RRS plans are to sustainably increase rural income, increase access to rural infrastructure and public services, and improve the living environment in rural areas. The national RRS plan phase 1 (2018?2022) focuses on consolidating and sustaining the poverty eradication gains, and has four pillars: (i) green agricultural development, (ii) agricultural modernization, (iii) rural infrastructure and public services, and (iv) rural governance. The national RRS phase 1 overlaps with the transition period (2021?2025), which also coincides with the 14th FYP (2021?2025). The PforR contributes to the achievement of the government's RRP, which is implemented in phased RRS plans. The Bank's PforR support focuses on three Results Areas (RAs): (i) RA1 ? Strengthening institutional capacity for governance to improve institutional coordination and management frameworks for results-based green agriculture and rural infrastructure development (wastewater and solid waste management systems); (ii) RA2 ? Greening selected agricultural value chains to sustainably increase rural income by adopting environmentally friendly production practices; and (iii) RA3 ? Increasing access to rural solid waste and wastewater services to improve the rural living environment and reduce pollutants. The PforR will support selected sub-programs under Pillar 1 (Green agricultural development) and Pillar 3 (Rural infrastructure and public services) of the government's RRS plan phase 1 (2018?2022), which overlaps with the 14th FYP (2021?2025).
To reduce regional disparities in learning outcomes, improve the retention of girls in upper primary education, and strengthen systems for delivering equitable education outcomes.

title.narrative: Improved retention of girls from poor and vulnerable populations, including in refugee populations, in junior school (grades 7, 8 and 9).

comment.narrative: The retention rate for girls in junior school who progressed from grade 7 to grade 8 in 2024 was 90.95 percent, according to NEMIS data, which tracks learners using their UPI numbers. This high retention rate is attributed to various interventions by the Ministry of Education (MoE) and its partners, aimed at encouraging students to stay in school and providing a supportive learning environment that protects them from external factors that could lead to distraction and dropout.

title.narrative: Targeted primary schools receiving school grants for completing priority areas in their SIPs

comment.narrative: The second (2nd) tranche of the RBSG funds has been disbursed to all 5,422 target schools. This disbursement was based on the achievement of DLR 1.2 — completion of implementation of at least three (3) out of the five (5) priority areas in the approved School Improvement Plan (SIP) — and partial achievement of DLR 1.3, which required that at least 70% of teachers were in class and teaching during the 2024 calendar year. All 5,422 schools received funds (USD 3000) for the achievement of DLR 1.2. Also, a total of 5,408 schools also received funding (USD 1500) under DLR 1.3, while 14 target schools did not meet this requiremennt.

This process is subsequently verified by the County or Sub County Directors of Education.
